groups.text: It is currently 18 degrees and partly cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Nvidia is negotiating an investment in Perplexity at a valuation exceeding 30 billion dollars. This figure represents a jump of more than 50 percent over the company's last funding round from a year ago. The surge follows a tripling of Perplexity's annualized revenue, which has climbed from 250 million to over 750 million dollars. This growth is driven in part by an AI agent for automated tasks called Perplexity Computer. While Nvidia previously considered an acqui-hire of the staff and technology, it now follows a pattern of investing in firms like Groq and Enfabrica. These investments often flow back to Nvidia as revenue when the portfolio companies purchase its chips. This potential deal comes as Perplexity CEO Aravind Srinivas considers an IPO around 2028. It also builds on a relationship established in March, when Perplexity joined Nvidia's Nemotron Coalition to promote open AI models against Chinese development efforts.

Russian attacks killed at least eight people and injured 43 across Ukraine as the country marked the 35th anniversary of its independence on August 24. The Ukrainian Air Force reports that Russia launched 143 drones and eight missiles overnight, including two Oniks anti-ship missiles and six guided air-launched Kh-31P and Kh-59 missiles. While air defenses downed 109 drones and five missiles, strikes hit 22 different locations. In Kharkiv Oblast, Russian drones struck railway infrastructure in the Lozova community, killing two women and seriously injuring an 11-year-old girl with burns. Governor Oleh Syniehubov noted that attacks across Kharkiv and 16 other settlements in the oblast killed five people and injured 17 others, including two children. In Donetsk Oblast, Russian attacks killed two additional people.

In Cameroon, 93-year-old President Paul Biya is working to secure his grip on power. Having led the country since 1982, he began his eighth term in 2025 and remains in office despite spending the last two and a half months in Geneva, Switzerland, where he continues to issue decrees. This effort to consolidate long-term control mirrors paths taken years ago by leaders in Russia and China. Meanwhile, Japan is investing in maritime technology through a new five-year subsidy program worth 15.1 billion yen. The transport and environment ministries will cover up to half the cost of equipment for ships powered by batteries, ammonia, or hydrogen to accelerate zero-emission orders. In the gaming world, Take-Two and Rockstar are pursuing legal action in U.S. courts to identify a leaker using the pseudonym Cyberleek. The companies are seeking information from Microsoft, Discord, and X after the individual released videos of GTA VI and profited via a memecoin.

Uber has been hit with a fine of over 824 million euros by the Dutch data protection authority for violating GDPR rules. The regulator found that Uber used an automated system to suspend drivers without any human review, leaving workers without income overnight. In a separate legal matter, TikTok has reached a 400 million dollar settlement with the U.S. Department of Justice over allegations it violated federal children's privacy laws. TikTok will pay 300 million dollars immediately and another 100 million once an order vacates a previous consent decree against its predecessor, Musical.ly. Meanwhile, maritime traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has dropped sharply due to U.S. and Iranian blockades. Fewer than 20 commodity vessels passed through the waterway over the weekend, though some ships may have avoided detection by switching off their transponders, including two empty very large crude carriers entering the Gulf.

Developers are refining how local AI models handle data to increase efficiency. In the latest release of llama.cpp, engineers updated mamba2 by flattening in and out projections. This change allows the system to dispatch GEMM instead of GEMV, while also removing a redundant output reshape. These technical adjustments aim to optimize performance across a wide range of hardware environments. The software now supports various platforms including Apple Silicon for macOS and iOS, as well as Ubuntu and Windows. It specifically integrates with CUDA 12 and 13 on Windows x64 and arm64 systems. Support also extends to openEuler x86 and aarch64 architectures using the 310p and 910b ACL Graph. By streamlining these mathematical operations, the project improves how open models run on everything from high-end GPUs to standard CPUs.

Tensions between France and Iran have escalated into a diplomatic standoff over the treatment of foreign officials. Iran's foreign ministry declared on Monday that France's decision to expel two Iranian diplomats is illegal. This move follows a sequence of retaliatory actions triggered by the brief arrest of two French diplomats in Tehran last July. Iranian officials accused those diplomats of interfering in internal affairs and subsequently banned them from returning to the country. In response, French Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot described the treatment of his colleagues as an intolerable act of intimidation. While Iran's ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei maintains that Tehran's original ban was a legal action, he admitted that France's retaliatory expulsions are not helpful to bilateral relations. The exchange marks a sharp decline in diplomatic ties between the two nations.

Iran-linked hackers shut down a British power plant for four days this past July. The attack caused real-world operational disruption and raised concerns about the resilience of Britain's distributed energy infrastructure. While official sources like the NCSC have remained quiet, the Telegraph broke the story on August 22nd. Experts warn that this expansion into the UK follows similar attacks by Iran-affiliated groups against military and critical infrastructure in the US, Israel, and several GCC states. In a separate diplomatic track, French President Emmanuel Macron is hosting Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed ben Salmane in Paris for two days of official talks. The visit focuses on diplomacy, regional issues, and economic contracts. Once isolated following the assassination of Jamal Khashoggi, the Crown Prince is now viewed by Paris as an essential partner in the Middle East.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be partly cloudy with temperatures between 18 and 24 degrees and no rain expected.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has the BLISS Reading Group at six forty-five in the evening, followed by Twerchhau at seven.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
